text:
maria: Quick heads-up — during a canary rollout we hit a routing mismatch where customers in eu-west fell back to an AMD-quantized variant that doesn't support tool-calling. Not critical yet but we need a compatibility contract.
jon: Ugh. Which policy allowed that route?
maria: It was a region-tier policy: tier=standard -> prefer cheapest compatible model, fallback order used variant-compat table that only checks architecture + token_limit, not tool-call capability.
kevin: So tokenizer + context length checks passed, but tool-calls failed at runtime?
maria: Exactly. The variant exposes different model signature so the call succeeds at tokenization but errors on function invocation with: `ERROR: missing tool_metadata`
tia: Can you paste the router logs? ops-bot attached the snippet earlier but here is the minimal stack: ```router: selected model redwood/gptx-quant-a region=eu-west variant=amd-q8 sequence=512
executor: model lacks tool_call_manifest -> raise ToolCallNotSupported
router: fallback policy=allow_fallback -> stop (no further fallbacks)```
sam: Why did router stop? We should have a policy to continue trying other variants or downgrade to hosted with tool-call compatibility.
jon: Current semantics: if fallback_target model exists but is missing required capabilities, router treats it as terminal unless `strict_capability_check=false`. That's the bug.
kevin: Proposed change: extend compatibility matrix to include a capabilities vector: [`tokenizer_family`, `max_context`, `tool_calling`, `function_schema_compat_v`]. Router must do an exact superset check for required capabilities.
maria: +1. Also need telemetry events when a fallback is selected but capability mismatch occurred. Right now we just log selection. Hard to surface to console.
tia: UX ask from devex: surface these mismatches in the rollout UI as "compatibility failures" with quick links to the diff between variants. devex: we'll need the capability vector in the rollout API response.
devex: can confirm — PMs want a toggle: "block fallbacks that degrade capabilities" and a visible metric in dashboards for "fallback-induced errors".
jon: Implementation concerns: computing tokenizer_family and function_schema comparison at route-time could be expensive. We only have model metadata in the registry. We could precompute compatibility pairs nightly and cache them.
kevin: I'd rather compute a compact bitmask for capabilities when models are onboarded, then route time is a single bitwise AND. Also store a compatibility_version number for invalidation.
infra-bot: note: nightly job `compat-update` will get a 30m window rebuild if we add new attributes.
sam: Fallback heuristics question: should we prefer region-local variant that lacks tool-calls over cross-region variant that supports them but adds +80ms latency? Product input needed.
maria: From customer tiering perspective: enterprise customers should avoid capability loss at all cost. Standard can accept it if latency savings > X tokens. We need policy knobs: `allow_capability_loss_for_tier = {standard: true, enterprise: false}` and a percent override.
kevin: Add router metrics: `fallback_attempt`, `fallback_capability_mismatch`, `fallback_success_after_retry`. Emit with tags: model_origin, candidate_variant, required_capabilities.
jon: Security note: tool-call parity must include verifying function_schema hash to avoid injection/contract mismatch. Add `function_schema_hash` to metadata.
tia: Also check context-length handling: some quantized variants chop input embeddings so effective context is 1-2 tokens lower for long prompts. That should be in capability vector as `effective_context_margin=2`.
maria: Action items: 1) spec compatibility vector (kevin, jon) 2) add capability bitmask to model registry and onboarding (infra) 3) router: strict superset check and retry logic (eng-platform) 4) telemetry+console: surface mismatches and provide toggle per-rollout (devex + product) 5) add unit tests & canary (maria)
sam: timeline?
kevin: I'll draft the spec by EOD. If infra can add bitmask fields in 72h, we can target a beta rollout next week.
infra-bot: ticket created: INFRA-7623 `model-capability-bitmask`
ops-bot: deploy alert: canary jobs showed 3 mismatch events in eu-west between 06:12-06:18 UTC, sample user ids included.
maria: Good catch. I'll open a quick rollback for that canary until we have the strict check in place.
devex: For the console change, we need example UI copy: "This fallback would remove tool calling — block fallback? [Allow]/[Block for tier]". We'll prototype.
jon: One more thing — we should version the compatibility matrix format and include migration steps. Backfills might be needed for historic models.
kevin: Agreed. Add `compat_schema_version` and migration plan.
maria: Thanks all. Keeping this thread for the implementation notes — I'll post PR links once ready. :thumbsup:
